nodes.summary: For finite sets of men and women of the same size and any strict preferences, there is a man-optimal stable matching. With the uniqueness statement, this makes "the" man-optimal stable mechanism of Roth's Theorem 5 well defined.
nodes.title: Every market with sides of equal size has a man-optimal stable matching

nodes.summary: A stable matching that no man likes less than any other stable matching (Gale and Shapley, *Amer. Math. Monthly* 69 (1962), Theorem 2; Roth, *Math. Oper. Res.* 7 (1982), Theorem 2).
nodes.title: Man-optimal stable matching

nodes.summary: A perfect matching is stable iff no man `m` and woman `w` are such that `m` prefers `w` to his partner and `w` prefers `m` to every man matched to her (that is, to her partner).
nodes.title: Stability without the inverse matching

nodes.summary: A mechanism whose outcome is stable for every stated profile (Roth, *Math. Oper. Res.* 7 (1982), §4, proof of Theorem 3: `h(P) ∈ C(P)` for every `P`).
nodes.title: Stable matching mechanism

nodes.summary: A matching mechanism `h` is strategy-proof when truthful revelation is a dominant strategy for every man and every woman: for every stated profile and every agent, replacing that agent's preference by any other strict order never yields a partner that the agent prefers, under the original preference, to the partner obtained by stating it.
nodes.title: Strategy-proof matching mechanism

nodes.summary: Whatever preferences the others state, no report `T` by man `m` gives him a partner he prefers, under his true preference `mp m`, to the partner he gets by reporting `mp m` (Roth, *Math. Oper. Res.* 7 (1982), §4, the paragraph before Theorem 3).
nodes.title: Truthful revelation is dominant for a man

nodes.summary: Whatever preferences the others state, no report `T` by woman `w` gives her a partner she prefers, under her true preference `wp w`, to the partner she gets by reporting `wp w` (Roth, *Math. Oper. Res.* 7 (1982), §4, the paragraph before Theorem 3).
nodes.title: Truthful revelation is dominant for a woman

nodes.summary: Let `h` be a matching mechanism that returns, for every stated profile, the man-optimal stable matching of that profile. Then truthful revelation is a dominant strategy for every man: no man can obtain a partner he truly prefers by misreporting, whatever the others state.
nodes.title: Strategy-proofness of the man-optimal stable mechanism for the men

nodes.summary: Two man-optimal stable matchings of the same profile are equal: if they gave some man different partners, his strict preference would rank one above the other, and the other matching would not be man-optimal.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the man-optimal stable matching

nodes.summary: A matching mechanism for men `M` and women `W` assigns a perfect matching between `M` and `W` to every stated profile of men's strict preferences over `W` and women's strict preferences over `M`. Roth calls it a matching procedure and identifies procedures that yield the same outcomes (Roth 1982, §4, remark after Corollary 5.1), which is why a mechanism is a function of the stated profile.
nodes.title: Matching mechanism

nodes.summary: No stable matching mechanism makes truthful revelation a dominant strategy for all agents. Formally, in the market with three men and three women (`Fin 3` on each side), there is no matching mechanism `h` such that `h(P)` is stable for every stated profile `P` and, for every man and every woman, no misreport ever yields a partner preferred under the agent's true preference.
nodes.title: Roth's impossibility theorem

nodes.summary: Let `μ` be the man-optimal stable matching of a market with at least one man. Then no perfect matching, stable or not, gives every man a partner he strictly prefers to his partner in `μ`. The assumption of a nonempty set of men excludes the empty market, where the condition "every man strictly prefers" holds vacuously. Roth's example after Corollary 5.1 shows that strong Pareto optimality fails: a matching can make…
nodes.title: Weak Pareto optimality of the man-optimal stable matching for the men

nodes.summary: `a` is preferred to `b` when `rk a < rk b`; an injective rank function gives a strict total order.
nodes.title: Preference given by a rank function

nodes.summary: Rank `0` for `a`, `1` for `b`, `2` otherwise.
nodes.title: The ranking `a ≻ b ≻ c` on three agents

nodes.summary: In Roth's market (men `m₁ : w₂ ≻ w₁ ≻ w₃`, `m₂, m₃ : w₁ ≻ w₂ ≻ w₃`; women `w₁ : m₁ ≻ m₃ ≻ m₂`, `w₂ : m₃ ≻ m₁ ≻ m₂`, `w₃ : m₁ ≻ m₂ ≻ m₃`), a perfect matching is stable if and only if it is `x = (m₁, w₂), (m₂, w₃), (m₃, w₁)` or `y = (m₁, w₁), (m₂, w₃), (m₃, w₂)`. The men prefer `x` and the women prefer `y`, with `m₂` and `w₃` indifferent. The proof checks all matchings by computation.
nodes.title: Roth's market has exactly the two stable matchings `x` and `y`

nodes.summary: After `m₁`'s misreport, `x` is the unique stable matching (Roth, *Math. Oper. Res.* 7 (1982), proof of Theorem 3: `C(P'') = {x}`).
nodes.title: After `m₁`'s misreport, `x` is the unique stable matching

nodes.summary: After `w₁`'s misreport, `y` is the unique stable matching (Roth, *Math. Oper. Res.* 7 (1982), proof of Theorem 3: `C(P') = {y}`).
nodes.title: After `w₁`'s misreport, `y` is the unique stable matching

nodes.summary: Man `m₁`'s misreport in Roth's market, `P''(m₁) : w₂ ≻ w₃ ≻ w₁` (Roth, *Math. Oper. Res.* 7 (1982), proof of Theorem 3).
nodes.title: Man `m₁`'s misreport in Roth's market

nodes.summary: Man `m₁`'s misreported preference `w₂ ≻ w₃ ≻ w₁` in Roth's market.
nodes.title: Man `m₁`'s misreported preference

nodes.title: Men's preferences in Roth's market

nodes.summary: Men's ranks in Roth's market (Roth, *Math. Oper. Res.* 7 (1982), proof of Theorem 3): `m₁ : w₂ ≻ w₁ ≻ w₃`, `m₂ : w₁ ≻ w₂ ≻ w₃`, `m₃ : w₁ ≻ w₂ ≻ w₃`.
nodes.title: Men's ranks in Roth's market

nodes.summary: Let `h` be a matching mechanism on three men and three women whose outcome is stable for every stated profile. At Roth's profile `P`, either man `m₁` obtains a partner he truly prefers by reporting `w₂ ≻ w₃ ≻ w₁`, or woman `w₁` obtains a partner she truly prefers by reporting `m₁ ≻ m₂ ≻ m₃`.
nodes.title: In Roth's market every stable mechanism is manipulable

nodes.summary: Woman `w₁`'s misreport in Roth's market, `P'(w₁) : m₁ ≻ m₂ ≻ m₃` (Roth, *Math. Oper. Res.* 7 (1982), proof of Theorem 3).
nodes.title: Woman `w₁`'s misreport in Roth's market

nodes.summary: Woman `w₁`'s misreported preference `m₁ ≻ m₂ ≻ m₃` in Roth's market.
nodes.title: Woman `w₁`'s misreported preference

nodes.summary: Women's preferences in Roth's market, from `rothWomenRank`.
nodes.title: Women's preferences in Roth's market

nodes.summary: Women's ranks in Roth's market (Roth, *Math. Oper. Res.* 7 (1982), proof of Theorem 3): `w₁ : m₁ ≻ m₃ ≻ m₂`, `w₂ : m₃ ≻ m₁ ≻ m₂`, `w₃ : m₁ ≻ m₂ ≻ m₃`.
nodes.title: Women's ranks in Roth's market

nodes.summary: `(m₁, w₂), (m₂, w₃), (m₃, w₁)` (Roth, *Math. Oper. Res.* 7 (1982), proof of Theorem 3).
nodes.title: The men-preferred stable matching `x` of Roth's market

nodes.summary: `(m₁, w₁), (m₂, w₃), (m₃, w₂)` (Roth, *Math. Oper. Res.* 7 (1982), proof of Theorem 3).
nodes.title: The women-preferred stable matching `y` of Roth's market

nodes.summary: For preferences on `Fin 3` given by rank functions `r` (men) and `s` (women), the stability condition of `isStable_iff_forall_partner` stated for a matching function `f`; it is decidable, which the proofs about Roth's market use.
nodes.title: Stability read off ranks on three agents

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
